title: Distance, Displacement and Velocity

standard_text: Distance and displacement; speed and velocity; describing motion using distance–time graphs. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 1, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): displacement, speed and velocity, describing motion, speed, velocity and graphs, motion graphs and average speed. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
body_html:
How to think about it

A scalar has only size (distance, speed, time); a vector has size and direction (displacement, velocity, acceleration). Displacement is the change in position; velocity = displacement/time; acceleration a = Δv/Δt.

On a position–time graph the gradient is the velocity; on a velocity–time graph the gradient is the acceleration and the area under the graph is the displacement. For constant acceleration: v = u + aΔt, Δx = uΔt + ½aΔt² and v² = u² + 2aΔx.

Example

A car goes from 0 to 20 m·s⁻¹ in 5 s. Acceleration?

a = Δv/Δt

Answer: 4 m·s⁻²

Example

You walk 3 m east and 3 m west. Displacement?

Directions cancel.

Answer: 0 m

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up distance and displacement.
  • Thinking a negative acceleration always means slowing down.
  • Reading the gradient of a position–time graph as acceleration.

faq.q: Can speed be constant while velocity changes?
faq.a: Yes, when the direction changes, for example moving in a circle.

items.q: Nonso drives 30 km in 0.5 h and then 51 km in 1 h. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 81 ÷ 1.5 = 54 km/h.

items.q: A runner covers 15 m in 5 s and then 60 m in 15 s. What is the average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 75 ÷ 20 = 3.75 m/s.

In which kind of collision is kinetic energy conserved?
c: a collision in which objects stick together
items.e: Momentum is conserved in all collisions.

items.q: What does Newton's third law state?
c: momentum is always lost in collisions
an object at rest stays at rest
if An exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A
items.e: The pair act on different objects.

items.q: A ball is dropped. Ignoring air resistance, what is its acceleration?
items.e: All objects fall with the same acceleration in a vacuum.

items.q: What does Newton's second law state?
c: the resultant force equals mass times acceleration, F = ma
objects keep moving unless a force acts
items.e: Acceleration is in the direction of the resultant force.

items.q: What is terminal velocity?
c: the constant speed reached when air resistance balances weight
the speed when an object hits the ground
items.e: Resultant force is zero.

items.q: A car brakes and a passenger without a seatbelt moves forwards. Why?

items.e: Seatbelts provide the force to slow the passenger.
